question: In which of the following processes is the pyruvate converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fermentation**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pyruvate is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide during fermentation: 
 
• Pyruvate is broken down to form ethanol and carbon dioxide
 
• Type of respiration
 
• Anaerobic respiration, which means it takes place in the absence of air (oxygen)
 
• Fermentation is a process that regenerates the electron carrier from the produced in glycolysis.
 
• The extra reactions in fermentation allow glycolysis to keep running by ensuring a steady supply of the electron carrier. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Diffusion
 
• The movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
 
• Diffusion is a passive process that occurs across membranes and over short distances.
 
• It's important for photosynthesis, as carbon dioxide diffuses into the leaves from the stomata.
 
• Diffusion also occurs during transpiration, when water and oxygen diffuse from the leaves into the environment. 
 
• Translocation
 
• The bulk movement of substances, such as organic compounds, through the vascular tissues of a plant over long distances.
 
• Translocation is an active and passive process that occurs in the xylem and phloem. 
 
• Transpiration
 
• The evaporation of water from the leaves of a plant in the form of water vapour.
 
• Transpiration can occur through the stomata or through the cuticle, a waxy covering on the surface of the leaves.
